clue.text: Group line should be held in general

indicators.note: the line letter is to be held inside the general's name, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: George Custer was the US cavalry general of Little Bighorn

explanation.surface: A military order: a line of troops must be kept under a general's command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an adjective ('in general') but is the noun: General Custer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster is a close bunch of similar things, a near synonym of a group.

clue.text: Strained party ends without regulars

parts.note: Labour is one of the two main UK political parties

indicators.note: dropping the regular (every second) letters of the word ends leaves the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A tense political party wraps up its meetings once the loyal regulars have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without regulars' removes the second and fourth letters of ENDS, leaving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboured effort or breathing is forced and difficult, the same as strained.

clue.text: Cheerful article penned by disturbed genius

indicators.note: the article is enclosed, as if in a pen, by the other letters
the letters of genius are disturbed, shaken into a new order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A troubled genius writes a cheerful piece for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' makes SGUINE; 'penned by' reads as writing, but means enclosed, as in a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine describes an optimistic, hopeful temperament, a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Cycle stocked by old worker is a rip-off

indicators.note: the cycle is the stock held within the other pieces, so it goes inside them

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
an orbit is one complete circuit, a cycle

explanation.surface: A bicycle sold in a shop staffed by a former employee turns out to be overpriced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link: the price described is exorbitant, that is, a rip-off.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorbitant charge is excessively high, which is what a rip-off price is.

clue.text: Region seeing a listener finally getting promoted

indicators.note: in a down clue, the final letter of the listener word is moved up to the top

parts.note: the ear is the organ you listen with

explanation.surface: A local area where an attentive staff member at last earns a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally getting promoted' moves the last letter R of EAR up to the front, giving REA.
explanation.definitionFit: Region and area both mean a part of a place or country.

clue.text: Universal anger about politician and judge

indicators.note: the anger is placed about, that is round after, the politician rather than before it as printed

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal
MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Everyone is furious with a politician, and a judge must rule on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning' in the surface but here tells you the anger follows the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire is the official who judges a game or contest, so judges as noun.

clue.text: The Queen perhaps may be working during month

indicators.note: the working word goes inside the month, as one thing happens during another

parts.note: March is a month
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: The Queen might be on duty through the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen regnant is an example of a sovereign ruler, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Always succeeded in case of rare defeat

indicators.note: the always and succeeded pieces sit in the casing letters
the case of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A team that always won finally suffers an unusual loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of rare' gives R and E, which wrap round EVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or defeat, especially in battle.

clue.text: Proper nozzle for watering a flower

parts.note: prim means correct and proper
the rose is the perforated spout on a watering can

explanation.surface: A gardener chooses the right spray head for watering a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The ROSE is the perforated spray head of a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower.

clue.text: Lack of restraint shown by a group performing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A band on stage plays with wild, uninhibited energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon as a noun means a wild freedom from inhibition.

clue.text: Beast from the east — and there without her to provide cover

indicators.note: in an across answer, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: an animal is a beast

indicators.note: the letters of her are taken out of there

explanation.surface: A wild creature from the east arrives, and with her gone something must offer shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' reverses ANIMAL to LAMINA; 'without her' strips HER from THERE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To laminate is to coat a surface with a protective layer of plastic or other material.

clue.text: Felt differently concerning small amounts of surplus food

indicators.note: felt is arranged differently, its letters reordered

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone has mixed feelings about the scraps left over after a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges FELT to LEFT; 'amounts of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers are uneaten food remaining after a meal, kept for later.

clue.text: A residential area may see problem rejected in advance

indicators.note: the reversed problem goes inside the advance word

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the rub is the problem, as in Hamlet's there's the rub

explanation.surface: A district might find a difficulty turned away before it arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' gives BUR; 'in advance' looks like 'beforehand' but advance is the noun, a loan on pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A suburb is an outlying district of a town, largely made up of homes.

clue.text: Popular criminal dealers welcoming the Queen's conclusions

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the dealers welcome the queen in among their letters

parts.note: fences deal in stolen goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; the 's is read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Popular villains who trade in stolen goods hosting the monarch: what is one to conclude?
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal dealers' is not an anagram signal: fences are receivers of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An inference is a conclusion reached by reasoning from evidence.

clue.text: A Democrat free to support province's team

indicators.note: in a down answer, the lower pieces support the upper one, so province comes first

parts.note: a realm is a province or domain
rid means free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: An American politician agrees to back a regional football side.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the pieces that 'support' REALM sit beneath it. Real Madrid is Spain's famous football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Real Madrid is a famous football club, an example of a sports team.

clue.text: Started to lose heart — and head!

indicators.note: losing the heart means dropping the middle letter of the word

parts.note: began means started

explanation.surface: Someone becomes discouraged and then loses their head too.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter G of BEGAN goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is informal slang for the head, as in a bump on the bean.

clue.text: Doctor able to speak and explain further

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of able are altered

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: A capable doctor holds forth and goes into more detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges ABLE to ELAB.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to add detail when explaining something.

clue.text: European role developed about tax that stops at different levels

indicators.note: the reworked role letters go about, round, the tax
role is developed into a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A European job grows to cover tax policy at several levels of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' turns ROLE into LEOR, which goes 'about' VAT as LE-VAT-OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift, called an elevator in the US, halts at each floor of a building.

clue.text: The race's over for such professionals

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over, turned into a new order

explanation.surface: The competition has ended, and these professionals are free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges the letters of THE RACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers are educators, the professionals whose working year is set by school terms.

clue.text: Talent that's good for British briskness

indicators.note: the good letter stands in for the British letter, a swap

parts.note: ability is talent

explanation.surface: A gift that serves Britain well brings speed and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for British' swaps the B of ABILITY for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Agility is quickness and nimbleness of movement, much as briskness is.

clue.text: Catchy phrases describing a name in high gloss

indicators.note: to describe a figure is to draw round it, so these letters go round the others
high, as in intoxicated, signals that gloss is in a disordered state

explanation.surface: Advertising slogans praise a brand with a high-gloss finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' rearranges GLOSS to SLOGS, which goes round AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Slogans are memorable phrases used in advertising or campaigns.

clue.text: Sort of look and stagger back

indicators.note: back means the stagger word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: A sideways glance that makes someone stumble backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, unpleasant glance, one particular kind of look.

clue.text: Current fixed terms must include answer after separation

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay follows after the separation word

parts.note: a gulf is a wide separation or gap

indicators.note: the answer letter is included inside the fixed letters
fixed, as in repaired, means terms is put into new order

explanation.surface: Contract terms after a split have to include a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges TERMS, and 'must include' places A inside: STREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf Stream is a warm ocean current flowing across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Small fish stink

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A tiny fish smells awful.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong foul smell, the same as a stink.

clue.text: Counsel notice moral shortcoming

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
a vice is a moral failing

explanation.surface: A lawyer notices a defect in someone's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a barrister but is used as a noun meaning guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel in the sense of guidance offered is a synonym of advice.

clue.text: Woody could be American, attached to foreign legion

indicators.note: the American letters are attached to the end of the reworked legion
foreign suggests something strange, so the letters of legion are changed

explanation.surface: A character called Woody might be an American who joined the Foreign Legion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges LEGION to LIGNEO; 'Woody' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ligneous is a technical word meaning made of or resembling wood.

clue.text: Capable of leading time — with oxygen!

parts.note: up means ahead or leading, as in a game
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An athlete able to set the pace, given an oxygen boost.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up to a task is to be equal to it, able to do it.

clue.text: Monk perhaps runs into trouble

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the trouble word

parts.note: bother means trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A monk finds himself in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes after the B of BOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Friars and monks address one another by this title, so a monk is an example.

clue.text: Determination of town on Etna destroyed

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another means it follows it
Etna is destroyed, broken into a new order of letters

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: The resolve of a town at the foot of a volcano that destroys it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' gives TENA; 'town on Etna' is tempting anagram fodder, but has too many letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is persistence and firmness of purpose, a synonym of determination.

clue.text: Turn one's attention to a day shift

parts.note: a shift is a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to focus on a single working day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' is not a work period but a straight, loose dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to deal with it or give it attention.
